source.snippet: I am building a local-first Mac writing app, and I am stuck on the story-memory layer. The problem: given a long fiction manuscript, I need to extract characters, aliases, relationships, locations, timeline facts, and unresolved plot facts. It has to work reasonably well across CJK and Latin-script text. For example, Chinese/Japanese/Korean names do not tokenize like English names, aliases may be implicit, and the same character can appear under several surface forms across chapters. [2026-06-28]

problem_statement: Developers building local-first writing or document apps for multilingual (CJK + Latin) audiences have no ready-made, offline-capable library or service for extracting named entities, relationships, and narrative facts from long-form text without bundling a large model.
target_segment: Indie developers and small software teams building writing, editing, or document intelligence apps targeting multilingual (especially East Asian) markets
notes: Single signal but the poster is explicitly a developer building a commercial product (a Mac writing app), which is a paying-buyer context. The gap is specific and technical: no existing lightweight offline library handles CJK+Latin NER well for narrative text. A productized API or embeddable library could charge per-seat or per-API-call to app developers. Willingness to pay is implied by commercial product context rather than stated explicitly — signal_strength capped at 2.
